official_title: Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 October 2003 establishing a scheme for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading within the Community and amending Council Directive 96/61/EC (Text with EEA relevance)
declared_regulatory_objective: Establish a greenhouse-gas emission allowance trading scheme to promote reductions cost-effectively and economically efficiently (Article 1).
regulatory_object: greenhouse-gas emissions and the allowance market linked to covered installations
principal_target_classes: operators of Annex I installations; persons holding or transferring allowances; Member States and their designated competent authorities as institutional implementers; new entrants and temporarily excluded installations as defined legal classes
principal_regulatory_authorities: European Commission; Member States and competent authorities; Central Administrator; committee assisting the Commission; independent verifiers; public as an information-access constituency
material_scope: Annex I activities and Annex II gases; permit, monitoring, reporting, verification, allocation, surrender, registry and penalty conditions; exclusions and thresholds in Annex I and Article 27
territorial_scope: Member States within the Community scheme; transfers may connect with third-country persons or schemes under Articles 12 and 25
temporal_scope: from 1 January 2005 through successive trading periods; entry into force on publication; review and expansion provisions in Article 30
principal_obligation_clusters: permit and scope control; national allocation plans and allocation; transfer/surrender/cancellation; monitoring/reporting/verification; registries and transaction control; penalties and public access; inclusion/exclusion, linking and review
main_governance_components: authorization; quantified allocation; market transfer and surrender; information production; independent verification; registry accounting; compliance and review
structural_logic: objective and scope -> permits and allocation -> monitoring/reporting -> verification -> surrender and cancellation -> registry control and penalties -> review, extension and links
evidence_basis: EXPLICIT_TEXT Articles 1-3, 4-21, 24-31 and Annexes I-V; CROSS_PROVISION_RECONSTRUCTION links Articles 4-16, 18-20 and Annexes I-V; ANALYTICAL_INFERENCE orientation from the integrated permit-market-compliance structure
analytical_uncertainty: original-act status and historical architecture mean later consolidated amendments are outside Phase 3; the Directive's interactions with later EU ETS instruments are not reconstructed here

official_title: Decision (EU) 2015/1814 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 6 October 2015 concerning the establishment and operation of a market stability reserve for the Union greenhouse gas emission trading scheme and amending Directive 2003/87/EC (Text with EEA relevance)
declared_regulatory_objective: Establish and operate a market stability reserve to address structural allowance supply-demand imbalances and make the EU ETS more resilient and orderly (recitals 4-6; Articles 1 and 3).
regulatory_object: the quantity and timing of EU ETS allowances entering or leaving auction supply through the market stability reserve
principal_target_classes: Member States responsible for auction volumes and shares; the Commission as publisher, monitor and reviewer; installations and market participants affected by auction supply; Union institutions receiving review proposals
principal_regulatory_authorities: European Commission; Member States; European Parliament and Council for amendments and review; auction platforms as operational market infrastructure identified by the Act
material_scope: EU ETS allowance supply, reserve placements/releases, auction calendars, unallocated allowances and consequential amendments to Directive 2003/87/EC
territorial_scope: Union EU ETS and Member State auctioning arrangements; references to the Union carbon market
temporal_scope: 2018 establishment; reserve operation from 1 January 2019; special placements in 2019-2020; transitional Directive rule until 31 December 2018; periodic review
principal_obligation_clusters: reserve establishment and quantified triggers; publication of total allowances in circulation; auction-calendar adjustment; consequential EU ETS amendments; monitoring and periodic review; transitional treatment
main_governance_components: market-balance measurement; reserve stock; rule-based supply adjustment; auction-calendar administration; review and legislative feedback
structural_logic: published circulation total -> formulaic reserve placement or release -> adjusted auction calendars -> Commission monitoring -> periodic review and possible amendment
declared_orientation: market-stabilization instrument within an EU ETS market-organization framework
evidence_basis: EXPLICIT_TEXT recitals 1-12 and Articles 1-5; CROSS_PROVISION_RECONSTRUCTION Articles 1(4)-(8), Article 2 and Article 3; ANALYTICAL_INFERENCE orientation from the reserve's quantified supply-adjustment design
analytical_uncertainty: the Decision presupposes the Directive 2003/87/EC auction architecture; this Phase 3 profile codes the Decision's own structure and not the full amended Directive

official_title: Regulation (EU) 2018/842 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 30 May 2018 on binding annual greenhouse gas emission reductions by Member States from 2021 to 2030 contributing to climate action to meet commitments under the Paris Agreement and amending Regulation (EU) No 525/2013 (Text with EEA relevance)
declared_regulatory_objective: Lay down Member State obligations for minimum contributions from 2021 to 2030 toward the Union target of a 30% reduction below 2005 levels in covered sectors and establish annual allocations and progress evaluation (Article 1).
regulatory_object: national greenhouse-gas emission levels and annual compliance allocations in non-ETS sectors
principal_target_classes: Member States as the directly obligated national units; Union institutions and technical bodies responsible for allocation, assessment, registry administration and implementation; national policy and reporting systems as the compliance context
principal_regulatory_authorities: European Commission; Central Administrator and Union Registry; European Environment Agency assisting assessment; Climate Change Committee; European Parliament and Council in review and legislative oversight
material_scope: IPCC energy, industrial processes and product use, agriculture and waste categories excluding Annex I Directive 2003/87/EC emissions; interactions with LULUCF and special treatment of civil aviation in Article 2
temporal_scope: 2021-2030 annual trajectory and 2030 limits; entry into force on the twentieth day after publication; reporting and review linked to Paris Agreement cycles
principal_obligation_clusters: binding 2030 limits and annual trajectory; Commission allocation and data review; borrowing, banking and transfer flexibilities; EU ETS and LULUCF flexibilities; corrective action and compliance checks; safety reserve; registry and delegated/implementing rulemaking; review and reporting
main_governance_components: target setting; inventory review; annual allocation; controlled flexibility; corrective action; compliance accounting; registry transparency; review
structural_logic: national emissions data -> Commission-reviewed annual allocations and linear trajectories -> permitted flexibilities -> annual monitoring and corrective action -> 2027/2032 compliance checks -> registry accounting and review
declared_orientation: binding national target-setting and compliance framework
evidence_basis: EXPLICIT_TEXT Articles 1-4, 8-17 and Annexes I-IV; CROSS_PROVISION_RECONSTRUCTION Articles 4-12 and the linked reporting provisions of Article 16; ANALYTICAL_INFERENCE orientation from binding allocations, flexibilities and compliance checks
analytical_uncertainty: the Regulation operates together with Regulations 2018/841
column19: 2018/1999 and Directive 2003/87/EC; this profile records those dependencies without reconstructing the external instruments

official_title: Regulation (EU) 2021/1119 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 30 June 2021 establishing the framework for achieving climate neutrality and amending Regulations (EC) No 401/2009 and (EU) 2018/1999 (‘European Climate Law’)
declared_regulatory_objective: Establish a framework for irreversible and gradual reduction of regulated anthropogenic emissions and enhancement of removals, with binding Union climate-neutrality by 2050 and an interim 2030 target (Article 1).
principal_regulatory_authorities: emissions and removals regulated in Union law
material_scope: and consistency of Union and national measures
territorial_scope: Union institutions; Member States; European Scientific Advisory Board on Climate Change; European Environment Agency; Commission-supported committees and national climate advisory bodies where established
temporal_scope: European Commission; European Parliament and Council; Scientific Advisory Board; Member States; EEA and Energy Union governance bodies
principal_obligation_clusters: anthropogenic emissions and removals by sources and sinks listed through Regulation 2018/1999 Annex V; climate neutrality, 2030 target, adaptation, scientific advice, assessments, public participation and sectoral roadmaps
main_governance_components: Union-wide and Member State climate governance; relevant national and Union measures; external Paris Agreement context
structural_logic: 2050 climate neutrality and negative emissions thereafter; binding 2030 net domestic reduction of at least 55% against 1990; future 2040 target process; recurring five-year and Paris global-stocktake reviews
declared_orientation: binding objectives and intermediate targets; scientific advice; adaptation strategy and national plans; collective and measure-consistency assessment; public participation; sectoral voluntary roadmaps; review; amendments to scientific and Energy Union governance
evidence_basis: goal setting; scientific assessment; adaptation planning; policy-consistency testing; collective progress review; public participation; sectoral dialogue; legislative feedback
analytical_uncertainty: 2050 objective and 2030 target -> scientific and adaptation framework -> Union and national measures -> Commission assessments of progress and consistency -> public/sectoral engagement -> review and future target adjustment
column19: framework-setting and review-oriented climate governance structure
column20: EXPLICIT_TEXT Articles 1-11 and 14; CROSS_PROVISION_RECONSTRUCTION Articles 3-8 and amendments in Articles 12-13; ANALYTICAL_INFERENCE orientation from the framework's target-science-assessment-review architecture
column21: the 2040 target is a mandated future legislative process rather than an operative target fixed by this original act; voluntary roadmaps and public participation are governance components but not binding sectoral obligations in this profile

official_title: Regulation (EU) 2023/955 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 10 May 2023 establishing a Social Climate Fund and amending Regulation (EU) 2021/1060
declared_regulatory_objective: Establish a Social Climate Fund for 2026-2032 to finance Member State Plans addressing the social impacts of extending greenhouse-gas emissions pricing to buildings and road transport (Articles 1 and 3).
regulatory_object: social impacts of building and road-transport carbon pricing and the allocation and use of Fund resources
principal_target_classes: vulnerable households; vulnerable micro-enterprises; vulnerable transport users; Member States submitting and implementing Plans; public/private implementing entities only as broad governed implementation classes
principal_regulatory_authorities: European Commission; Member States; European Parliament and Council in transparency
material_scope: review and oversight; audit and anti-fraud institutions named in Article 21; local and regional authorities and consulted stakeholders within Plan governance
territorial_scope: Fund-supported measures, Plans, allocations, building renovation, heating/cooling decarbonisation, mobility, temporary direct income support, milestones, targets, monitoring, payment and financial controls
temporal_scope: Member States and Union implementation levels
principal_obligation_clusters: Fund period 2026-2032; application from 30 June 2024; payments by 31 December 2033; Plan completion indicators through 31 July 2032; evaluations in 2025-cycle and ex post by 31 December 2033
main_governance_components: Plan preparation and consultation; eligibility and measures/investments; financial allocation and national contribution; Commission assessment and decision; milestone-conditioned payments, suspension and termination; internal controls and anti-fraud; coordination and transparency; monitoring and evaluation
structural_logic: social-impact assessment; participatory Plan design; targeted investment and temporary support; direct Union financial management; milestone-based disbursement; audit/data systems; coordination and public transparency
declared_orientation: carbon-price impact and vulnerability assessment -> consulted Social Climate Plan -> Commission relevance/effectiveness/efficiency/coherence assessment -> approved measures and milestones -> payments on verified achievement -> monitoring, audit, transparency and evaluation
analytical_uncertainty: EXPLICIT_TEXT Articles 1-3, 4-8, 10-12, 14-27 and Annexes I-V; CROSS_PROVISION_RECONSTRUCTION Articles 4-6, 16-21 and 24-27; ANALYTICAL_INFERENCE orientation from Plan approval, conditional financing and control architecture
column19: the volume and timing of Fund resources depend partly on Directive 2003/87/EC provisions outside this act; Article 9 permits implementation through other public/private entities but Phase 3 does not classify intermediary roles
